uncited: It differs from [Orthographic (Parallel) Camera Ray Generation](1319-orthographic-parallel-camera-ray-generation.md) by supporting perspective projection (converging rays) and from [Pinhole Camera Ray Generation](5058-pinhole-camera-ray-generation.md) by explicitly constructing and utilizing camera parameters (intrinsic/extrinsic or basis vectors) rather than assuming a canonical pinhole model [S2172, S5058].
It serves as the foundational step for [Ray Casting](6080-ray-casting.md) and [Ray Marching](3487-compute-shader-ray-marching-setup.md).
The computation involves a constant number of vector operations and matrix multiplications.
Only local variables and camera parameters are needed.
Each thread computes one ray independently.
On GPUs, coalesced memory access to camera matrices (uniforms) is critical [Parent].
It bridges the gap between 2D rasterization coordinates and 3D geometric space.

The claim states that 'Near/Far' are clipping plane distances used for matrix generation. The evidence in Source [S4] explicitly shows the construction of projection matrices using `mat4.perspective(..., 1/8, 512.0)`. These matrices (`lightTransform`, `proj`) are used for rendering (matrix generation), not directly for ray direction calculation in the context of the claim's distinction. Therefore, the evidence supports the claim.

*   Basis vectors: right $\mathbf{u}$, up $\mathbf{v}$, forward $\mathbf{w}$ (or view direction) [S5, S6, unofficial].

The claim states that the basis vectors are defined as right u, up v, and forward w (or view direction). Source [S5] explicitly defines the camera using basis vectors u, v, w and provides the ray direction calculation `s = vp_x * u + vp_y * v - dist * w`. In standard computer graphics conventions (and implied by the negative sign on `w` when calculating the ray direction from the eye position towards the view plane), `u` corresponds to the right vector, `v` to the up vector, and `w` to the forward (view) direction. Source [S6] describes a different method using inverse view matrices and clip-space coordinates, but it does not contradict the definition in [S5]; it simply offers an alternative implementation. Since the claim accurately reflects the definitions and usage found in Source [S5], the evidence supports the claim.
